blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) are essential for modern industrial Computer-Aided Design (CAD). However, existing autoregressive SVG generation models are predominantly tailored for artistic creation and struggle to maintain the rigorous geometric fidelity and cross-view spatial alignment required for engineering drawings. To bridge this gap, we introduce DrawingsDreamer , a unified Large Language Model (LLM)-driven framework for multi-view vector-based engineering drawings generation. By formulating the generation of multi-view engineering drawings purely as a sequence modeling task, we eliminate the need of raster image encoders. We propose a Streamlined Representation utilizing hierarchical postfix tokenization, which guides the model to establish local geometric coordinates before assigning semantic boundaries. Optimized via a progressive task-aware curriculum schedule, DrawingsDreamer effectively transitions from localized structural repair to macroscopic generation in a unified model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our unified model achieves strong performance in both geometric fidelity and syntactic accuracy across diverse conditional and unconditional generation tasks.
blocks.zh: 可缩放矢量图形(SVG)对于现代工业计算机辅助设计(CAD)至关重要. 然而,现有的自旋式SVG生成模型主要针对艺术创作和斗争,以保持工程图画所需的严格的几何忠诚度和跨视空间对齐. 为了弥补这一差距,我们引入了DratingsDreamer,一个统一的大语言模型(LLM)驱动的框架,用于基于多视图矢量的工程绘图生成. 通过将多景工程图画的生成纯粹作为一个序列建模任务,我们消除了光栅图像编码器的需求. 我们提议采用分级的后缀符号化,简化表示方式,指导在划定语义边界之前建立本地几何坐标的模型。 通过渐进式任务感知课程表优化,DratingsDreamer在统一模式下从局部结构修复有效过渡到宏图生成. 广泛的实验证明,我们的统一模型在各种有条件和无条件的生成任务中,在几何忠诚度和合成精确度两方面都取得了强大的性能.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) have long served as the de facto standard in modern digital design, spanning applications from user interfaces (UI) to complex industrial Computer-Aided Design (CAD) systems. Their widespread adoption is driven by resolution independence, compact file sizes, and the capacity for precise, parametric control over geometric primitives such as polygons and Bézier curves. While recent advancements in generative AI have revolutionized visual synthesis, the creation of highly structured, multi-view engineering drawings remains a formidable challenge. As the foundation of modern manufacturing, engineering drawings demand strict structural validity, exact geometric parameterization, and rigorous cross-view spatial alignment. These qualities differ fundamentally from the requirements of general artistic creation.
blocks.zh: 可缩放矢量图形(SVG)长期以来一直作为现代数字设计中事实上的标准,从用户界面(UI)到复杂的工业计算机辅助设计(CAD)系统的应用跨越. 它们的广泛采用是由分辨率独立,紧凑的文件大小,以及对几何原始物如多边形和贝塞尔曲线进行精确,参数控制的能力所驱动的. 虽然最近基因AI的进步使视觉合成发生了革命性的变化,但制作高度结构化的多视图工程图纸仍然是一个艰巨的挑战. 作为现代制造的基础,工程图纸要求严格的结构有效性,精确的几何参数化,严格的交叉视野空间对齐. 这些品质与一般艺术创作的要求根本不同.

blocks.en: Existing approaches to SVG generation largely fall short of these industrial demands. Optimization-based methods [ 36 , 29 ] often struggle with prohibitive computational overhead and tend to produce unstructured, dense anchor points that destroy the editability inherent to the SVG format. Conversely, autoregressive methods and LLM-driven pipelines [ 48 , 1 , 62 ] have demonstrated remarkable scalability by treating SVG generation as a sequence modeling task. However, bottlenecked by limited context lengths and training corpora overwhelmingly skewed towards artistic domains (e.g., icons, fonts, and illustrations) [ 59 , 41 ] , these models fail to capture the long-range coordinate dependencies and spatial constraints required for engineering CAD drafts. Concurrently, the broader CAD generation community has predominantly focused on synthesizing 3D Boundary Representations (BRep) or meshes from point clouds and images [ 57 , 61 ] , leaving the direct generation of the 2D drawings themselves entirely unexplored.
blocks.zh: 现有的SVG生成方法基本没有达到这些工业需求. 基于优化的方法[36,29]往往与令人望而却步的计算间接费用相搏,往往产生无结构,密集的锚点,破坏SVG格式所固有的可编辑性. 反之,自旋方法和LLM驱动的管道[48, 1, 62]通过将SVG生成作为序列建模任务,表现出显著的可伸缩性. 然而,由于上下文长度有限,培训公司绝对偏向艺术领域(如图标、字体和插图)[59,41],这些模型未能捕捉到CAD工程草案所需的远程坐标依赖性和空间限制。 与此同时,更广泛的CAD一代社区主要侧重于从点云和图像合成3D边界代表物(BREP)或中间体[57,61],使得直接生成的2D绘图本身完全没有被探索.

blocks.en: Aligning with the broader consensus that scalable, general-purpose sequence modeling ultimately outpaces hand-crafted optimization heuristics, we frame the synthesis of 3D engineering drawings purely as a 2D sequence generation paradigm. In this paper, we propose DrawingsDreamer , the first unified multi-view engineering drawings generation model. By projecting 3D CAD objects into a canonical set of principal views, we deliberately avoid harnessing any raster image encoders. Instead, we rely entirely on the robust spatial reasoning capabilities of LLMs operating over discrete coordinate tokens. To effectively map continuous geometric spaces to discrete vocabularies, we introduce a Streamlined Representation featuring a novel hierarchical postfix tokenization strategy. This formulation compels the model to robustly establish continuous local coordinates prior to encapsulating them with semantic boundaries, thereby stabilizing the generation of complex spatial structures.
blocks.zh: 与可伸缩的,通用的序列模型最终超过手工制造的优化 Heuristics 的更广泛的共识一致,我们把三维工程图纸的合成完全作为二维序列生成范式. 在本文中,我们提出了DratingsDreamer,这是第一个统一的多景工程绘图生成模型. 通过将3D CAD 对象投影成一组主视图,我们刻意避免利用任何光栅图像编码器. 相反,我们完全依赖LLMS在离散坐标符上运行的强大空间推理能力。 为了有效地将连续几何空间映射到离散词汇中,我们引入了一种精简的表示方式,其特点是一种新的等级后缀符号化战略。 这种配体迫使模型在用语义边界封装之前,要牢固地建立连续的局部坐标,从而稳定复杂空间结构的生成.

blocks.en: To facilitate the training of our model, we systematically construct a multi-view aligned engineering drawings corpus by rendering standard projections from existing 3D CAD collections. Leveraging this structured data, we optimize DrawingsDreamer through a progressive, task-aware curriculum schedule, empowering a single unified model to seamlessly transition between microscopic topological repair, partial view completion, and unconstrained macroscopic drawings imagination.
blocks.zh: 为了便利对我们的模型进行培训,我们通过从现有的3D CAD收藏中作出标准预测,系统地构建了多视图对齐的工程图集。 利用这种结构化的数据,我们通过一个渐进的,任务感知的课程表来优化DratingsDreamer, 赋予一个单一的统一模型在微观地形修复,部分视图完成和不受约束的宏观绘图想象之间无缝过渡的能力。

blocks.en: In summary, our core contributions are as follows:
blocks.zh: 总之,我们的核心贡献如下:

blocks.en: • We propose a Streamlined Representation utilizing a hierarchical postfix tokenization strategy. This formulation effectively maps continuous geometric spaces into a discrete, LLM-friendly vocabulary, fundamentally stabilizing the autoregressive generation of complex spatial coordinates. • We introduce DrawingsDreamer , the first unified framework capable of generating highly structured, multi-view parametric engineering drawings. By optimizing the model via a progressive, task-aware curriculum schedule, we empower a single framework to seamlessly transition between microscopic topological repair and macroscopic spatial generation. • Extensive evaluations demonstrate that DrawingsDreamer achieves state-of-the-art performance in both geometric fidelity and syntactic accuracy across diverse conditional and unconditional multi-view generation tasks.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 SVG Generation
blocks.zh: 2.1 SVG 生成

blocks.en: The automated generation of vector graphics has witnessed a significant paradigm shift from instance-level optimization to large-scale sequence modeling. Early optimization methods [ 36 , 29 ] iteratively refine SVG parameters by minimizing photometric loss via differentiable rasterizers. However, these approaches rely heavily on iterative optimization for individual instances. Consequently, they suffer from prohibitive computational overhead and often yield unstructured outputs lacking geometric fidelity. In contrast, driven by the shift towards large-scale data and general-purpose computation, learning-based SVG generation has witnessed significant progress. Advancements range from the curation of extensive vector datasets [ 54 , 7 , 20 , 63 ] to the development of generative pipelines built upon RNNs [ 44 , 13 , 40 , 16 ] and VAEs [ 5 , 34 , 46 , 45 , 47 ] . More recently, the paradigm has shifted towards treating SVG generation as a sequence modeling task by leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) [ 48 , 1 , 62 , 8 , 49 ] , which demonstrate exceptional generative flexibility across diverse domains [ 25 , 67 , 43 , 66 , 17 , 12 , 9 ] .
blocks.zh: 矢量图形的自动化生成见证了从实例级优化到大规模序列模型化的重大范式转变. 早期优化方法[36,29] 迭代完善SVG参数,通过不同光栅将光度损失最小化. 然而,这些方法在很大程度上依赖于单个实例的迭代优化。 因此,它们承受着令人望而却步的计算间接费用,而且往往产生缺乏几何忠诚的无结构产出。 相比之下,由于转向大规模数据和通用计算,基于学习的SVG生成工作取得了重大进展。 从研究广泛的矢量数据集[54, 7, 20, 63]到开发基于RNNs[44, 13, 40, 16]和VAEs[5, 34, 46, 45, 47]的基因管道,都取得了进步. 最近,这一范式已转向将SVG生成作为一种序列建模任务,利用大语言模型[48、1、62、8、49],这些模型在不同的领域表现出特殊的遗传灵活性[25、67、43、66、17、12、9]。

blocks.en: Despite these advances, existing LLM-driven SVG generation models [ 59 , 41 , 56 , 63 ] remain bottlenecked by limited context lengths and training corpora restricted to artistic or visual creation. Consequently, generating highly structured engineering drawings with aligned multiview representations remains an unexplored frontier, limiting the adoption in professional CAD workflows. To bridge this gap, we propose the first unified framework for generating consistent multiview parametric engineering drawings, effectively scaling these capabilities to complex industrial applications.
blocks.zh: 尽管取得了这些进步,但现有的LLM驱动的SVG生成模型[59,41,56,63]仍然受到限于艺术或视觉创作的有限上下文长度和培训公司的限制. 因此,制作结构严密的工程图纸以及统一的多视图图纸仍然是未探索的前沿,限制了专业的CAD工作流程的采用。 为了弥补这一差距,我们提议建立第一个统一的框架,以生成一致的多视图参数工程图纸,有效地将这些能力扩大到复杂的工业应用。

blocks.en: 2.2 Computer-Aided Design
blocks.zh: 2.2 计算机辅助设计

blocks.en: The domain of Computer-Aided Design (CAD) has rapidly evolved from foundational datasets [ 57 , 21 , 55 ] to sophisticated generative pipelines [ 28 , 60 , 26 , 23 , 27 , 58 , 2 , 57 , 61 , 24 , 33 , 18 , 42 , 6 , 30 , 51 , 2 , 64 , 19 ] . Current methods predominantly focus on reverse engineering, generating Boundary Representation (BRep) models from modalities like point clouds [ 57 , 61 , 24 , 33 , 18 , 42 ] , images [ 6 , 30 ] , or text [ 51 , 2 , 64 , 19 ] .

Furthermore, while some techniques reconstruct CAD models from static engineering drawings [ 11 , 22 , 32 , 52 , 10 , 4 , 14 , 38 , 53 , 65 , 39 ] , generating the drawings themselves remains entirely unexplored. As the fundamental blueprints of modern manufacturing, automating the creation of these drawings represents a critical missing link. To address this void and facilitate the training of generative models, we establish a scalable pipeline to derive structured, multi-view aligned 2D drawings directly from standard 3D CAD databases.
blocks.zh: 此外,虽然有些技术从静态工程图纸中重建CAD模型[11、22、32、52、10、4、14、38、53、65、39],但图纸本身仍然完全没有得到探讨。 作为现代制造业的基本蓝图,这些图画的创作自动化代表了关键的缺失环节. 为了解决这一空虚问题并促进基因模型的培训,我们建立了一个可伸缩的管道,直接从标准3D CAD数据库中得出结构化,多视图对齐的2D图纸.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: In this section, we present the architecture and training pipeline of DrawingsDreamer . We first introduce our Streamlined Representation (Section 3.1 ), which employs a hierarchical postfix tokenization scheme to effectively map continuous parametric geometries into a discrete, LLM-friendly vocabulary. Building upon this formulation, we then detail our unified instruction-tuning paradigm and progressive task-aware curriculum schedule (Section 3.2 ). This dynamic optimization strategy empowers a single foundation model to seamlessly master both microscopic topological validity and rigorous cross-view spatial alignment.
blocks.zh: 我们在此介绍DratingsDreamer的架构和培训管道。 我们首先采用简化代表法(第3.1节),采用分级的后缀符号化办法,有效地将连续的参数几何图案映射成一个离散的、方便LLM的词汇。 在此基础上,我们详细介绍了我们的统一教学调整模式和逐步了解任务的课程安排(第3.2节)。 这种动态优化策略授权一个单一的基础模型,可以无缝地掌握微观地形有效性和严格的交叉视野空间对齐.

blocks.en: 3.1 Streamlined Representation for Multi-View Engineering Drawings
blocks.zh: 3.1 多维工程绘图的精简代表

blocks.en: To effectively harness the scaling capabilities of LLMs for engineering drawings generation, we formulate the synthesis of engineering drawings as a pure sequence modeling paradigm. Specifically, a 3D CAD object ℳ \mathcal{M} is projected into a canonical set of four principal views 𝒱 = { v front , v right , v top , v iso } \mathcal{V}=\{v_{\text{front}},v_{\text{right}},v_{\text{top}},v_{\text{iso}}\} . This projection provides a complete, unambiguous geometric description while deliberately avoiding the computational overhead associated with rendering and processing rasterized images via visual encoders. We encode this geometry into a Streamlined Representation , a compact training format optimized purely for LLM comprehension.
blocks.zh: 为了有效地利用LLMS的缩放能力来进行工程图纸的生成,我们把工程图纸的合成作为纯粹的序列建模范式. 具体来说,3D CAD 对象 M\ mathcal{M} 被投射成由四个主视图 V = { v 前, v 右, v 上, v 异构 }\ mathcal{ V}=\{v_{\text{ 前,v_{\text{右,v_{\text{top}},v_{\text{iso}}\}}组成的套装. 这种投影提供了完整,毫不含糊的几何描述,同时刻意避免通过视觉编码器渲染和处理光栅化图像相关的计算间接费用. 我们把这个几何编码成一个精简的表示, 一种精密的训练格式, 完全为了LLM的理解。

blocks.en: Figure 2: Visualization of the Streamlined Representation, detailing its hierarchical data organization. Continuous coordinates are grouped into primitive boundaries (e.g., lines and curves), formed into closed loops, and ultimately structured into unified view-level sequences.
blocks.zh: 图 2:可视化精简代表,详细列出其分级数据组织. 连续坐标被组合成原始边界(如线和曲线),形成闭环,最终形成统一的视级序列.

blocks.en: While prior works typically adopt a prefix-based tokenization scheme [ 63 ] , we introduce a hierarchical postfix tokenization strategy. The model is compelled to first regress the geometric coordinates, subsequently encapsulating them with a semantic boundary token (e.g., <end_curve> ). To maintain a streamlined vocabulary and reduce the model token search space, the standard SVG close path command ( Z or z ) is not assigned a unique token. Instead, our parser explicitly converts it into a line sequence connecting the current position back to the subpath starting coordinate, terminated by <end_line> . The geometric definitions of our structural vocabulary are summarized in Table 1 .
blocks.zh: 前作一般采用基于前缀的标注方案[63],而我们则采用层次化的后缀标注策略. 该模型必须首先递归几何坐标,然后用语义边界符号(例如: " end_curve " )封装这些坐标。 为了保持精简的词汇,并缩小模型令牌搜索空间,标准SVG关闭路径指令(Z或z)没有指定一个独特的令牌. 相反,我们的解析器明确将其转换为连接当前位置回向子路径起始坐标的线条序列,终止于<end_line> 。 表1概述了我国结构词汇的几何定义。

blocks.en: To empower the LLM with comprehensive multi-view spatial reasoning, we cast all generation sub-tasks detailed in Table 2 into a unified prediction framework, as illustrated in Figure 3 . Rather than training specialized models, we employ a single pre-trained Llama-family [ 48 ] causal language model. To achieve this efficiently, we apply Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) [ 15 ] alongside standard instruction-tuning practices. Specifically, we compute the cross-entropy loss ℒ \mathcal{L} exclusively over the generative target S target S_{\text{target}} : ℒ = − ∑ t = 1 | S target | log P ( x t ∣ x < t , ℐ , S context ; Θ ) , \mathcal{L}=-\sum_{t=1}^{|S_{\text{target}}|}\log P(x_{t}\mid x_{<t},\mathcal{I},S_{\text{context}};\Theta), (2) where Θ \Theta denotes the trainable LoRA parameters. By masking the instruction ℐ \mathcal{I} and context S context S_{\text{context}} during optimization, this unified objective allows the model to seamlessly alternate between diverse generation modes within the same training batch without gradient interference.

blocks.en: Empirical evidence suggests that directly optimizing LLMs on complex, weakly-conditioned spatial generation tasks often leads to sub-optimal convergence and hallucinated topologies [ 3 , 50 ] . To address this, we introduce a progressive, task-aware curriculum schedule that dynamically adjusts the sampling distribution of tasks across training epochs.
blocks.zh: 经验证据表明,在复杂,条件薄弱的空间生成任务上直接优化LLMs往往导致次优化的趋同和幻觉的地形[3,50]. 为了解决这个问题,我们采用了一种渐进的、意识到任务的课程时间表,动态地调整各个培训阶段任务抽样分布。

blocks.en: Crucially, we treat Unconditional Generation ( ∅ → 𝒱 \emptyset\rightarrow\mathcal{V} ) as a continuous base task. Its sampling weight remains continuously active throughout the entire training process to robustly anchor the model’s fundamental data distribution and generative capacity. Concurrently, the distribution of the remaining conditional tasks follows a smoothed optimization trajectory spanning three progressive stages:
blocks.zh: 关键是,我们把无条件生成(QQ ~ V\demptyset\rightarrow\ mathcal{V})视为一个连续的基础任务. 其取样权重在整个培训过程中始终保持活跃,以强有力地巩固模型的基本数据分布和遗传能力。 同时,其余有条件任务的分布遵循跨越三个渐进阶段的平滑优化轨迹:

blocks.en: • Stage I: Local Syntax and Topology (Early Epochs). The conditional sampling distribution heavily favors microscopic structural tasks, specifically Path Level Semantic Masking . This initial phase compels the model to establish robust coordinate syntax and localized geometric priors before tackling complex global spatial reasoning. • Stage II: Partial View Alignment (Middle Epochs). As local geometric stability is acquired, we dynamically shift the conditional weights towards Partial View Completion (e.g., inferring two missing orthographic views given the isometric and one available orthographic view). This stage forces the model to learn cross-view spatial alignment and correlation anchored by strong contextual cues. • Stage III: Global Spatial Translation (Late Epochs). In the final stage, the distribution transitions predominantly to macroscopic spatial tasks, specifically Iso-to-Ortho and Ortho-to-Iso translations. Having progressively mastered local topology and partial alignment, the model is now optimized for rigorous 3D structural reasoning and deterministic projective geometry inference from highly compressed contexts.

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验设置

blocks.en: Implementation Details. We instantiate DrawingsDreamer using LLaMA-3.2-3B [ 37 ] as the base LLM, chosen for its strong sequence modeling capabilities and competitive performance among open-source foundation models. To ensure parameter-efficient fine-tuning, we employ LoRA [ 15 ] with a rank of r = 8 r=8 and α = 32 \alpha=32 . Our dataset is constructed from DeepCAD [ 57 ] , comprising 178,238 valid CAD models. We split the dataset at the CAD-model level into 160,414 training, 8,912 validation, and 8,912 test models, corresponding to a 90%/5%/5% split. For the hardware setup, models with parameters up to 3B are trained on a cluster of eight NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPUs, while larger models are trained on eight NVIDIA L40 GPUs. We employ the AdamW optimizer [ 35 ] with a batch size of 16. We apply a cosine annealing learning rate schedule initialized at 5 × 10 − 4 5\times 10^{-4} and train the model for 15 epochs.

blocks.en: 4.2 Metrics
blocks.zh: 4.2 计量

blocks.en: To evaluate both the syntactic correctness and geometric fidelity of our generated outputs, we employ a comprehensive protocol tailored to distinct task categories.
blocks.zh: 为了评估我们产出的协同正确性和几何忠诚性,我们采用了一个适合不同任务类别的全面协议。

blocks.en: For translation and completion tasks (Iso-to-Ortho, Ortho-to-Iso, and Partial View Completion), we evaluate performance across three levels. Syntactically, we compute Command Accuracy ( Acc cmd \text{Acc}_{\text{cmd}} ) and Parameter Accuracy ( Acc params \text{Acc}_{\text{params}} ) to assess the exact match rate of structural tokens and the precision of numerical coordinates, respectively. Visually, we report PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS on rasterized 2D multi-view SVGs. Geometrically, we evaluate cross-view geometric fidelity by uniformly sampling point clouds from the geometric paths of the generated SVGs across different views and computing the Chamfer Distance (CD) between them.
blocks.zh: 对于翻译和完成的任务(Iso-to-Ortho,Ortho-to-Iso,以及部分视图完成),我们评价三个级别的业绩. 在战术上,我们分别计算命令精确度(Acc cmd\ text{Acc\text{cmd})和参数精确度(Acc params\ text{Acc\text{params}),以评估结构符的确切匹配率和数字坐标的精确度. 视觉上,我们报告PSNR,SSIM,和LPIPS的光栅化2D多视图SVG. 从几何角度来说,我们通过从不同观点产生的SVG的几何路径中统一取样点云来评价交叉视图几何忠诚度,并计算它们之间的Chamfer距离。

blocks.en: For this task, we measure the diversity and distributional alignment of the generated drawings against the dataset. Following standard shape generation protocols [ 57 ] , we report Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD), Coverage (COV), and Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD).
blocks.zh: 为此,我们对照数据集衡量生成的图纸的多样性和分布一致性。 遵循标准形状生成协议[57],我们报告Jensen-Shannon Difference(JSD),覆盖范围(COV)和最大平均差(MMD).

blocks.en: Compared to training specialized models for isolated tasks (e.g., { v iso } → 𝒱 ortho \{v_{\text{iso}}\}\rightarrow\mathcal{V}_{\text{ortho}} ), our unified multitask paradigm consistently achieves superior performance. blocks.en: Replacing our progressive three-stage curriculum with random task sampling leads to sub-optimal convergence and degraded Chamfer Distance. blocks.en: Removing this microscopic structural task during training degrades geometric fidelity and command accuracy in the generated multiview sequences. Forcing the model to explicitly learn basic geometric structures serves as a crucial stepping stone for coherent macroscopic generation.
blocks.zh: 在训练中消除这一微缩结构任务会降低生成的多视图序列中的几何忠诚度和命令精度。 强迫该模型明确学习基本的几何结构,是连贯的宏观生成的关键基石。

blocks.en: Replacing our hierarchical postfix tokenization with standard prefix representations (e.g., M , L , C sequencing) drops parameter accuracy. Regressing coordinates before assigning semantic boundaries aligns better with the innate sequence modeling capabilities of causal LLMs in engineering drawing scenarios.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: In this paper, we introduced DrawingsDreamer , a unified generative framework that frames multi-view engineering drawing synthesis as a pure sequence modeling task. By leveraging a streamlined representation with hierarchical postfix tokenization and a progressive task-aware curriculum, our approach effectively captures rigorous cross-view spatial alignments and complex geometric dependencies. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that DrawingsDreamer sets a new state of the art in generating geometrically precise parametric engineering drawings. We anticipate that expanding its geometric vocabulary to support more complex parametric constraints will further advance the integration of general-purpose sequence modeling into professional AI-assisted industrial design workflows.
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们引入了DratingsDreamer(DragingsDreamer),一个统一的基因框架,将多视图工程绘图合成作为纯粹的序列建模任务. 通过利用具有分级后缀符号化和渐进任务意识课程的精简代表,我们的方法有效地抓住了严格的跨视图空间对接和复杂的几何依赖。 广泛的评价表明,DigingsDreamer在生成几何精确的参数工程图纸方面设定了一种新的艺术状态. 我们预计,扩大其几何词汇以支持更复杂的参数限制将进一步推动将通用序列模型纳入专业AI辅助工业设计工作流程.

blocks.en: To investigate the impact of fundamental Large Language Model capacity on spatial reasoning and multi-view alignment, we extend our framework by scaling DrawingsDreamer up to a 7B parameter architecture (e.g., LLaMA-3-7B).
blocks.zh: 为了调查基本大语言模型能力对空间推理和多视图对齐的影响,我们通过将DratingsDreamer放大到7B参数架构(如LLaMA-3-7B)来扩展我们的框架.

blocks.en: While our primary experiments utilize a 3B parameter model for an optimal balance between performance and computational efficiency, generating highly structured engineering blueprints demands rigorous logical deduction and precise coordinate regression. By scaling up the backbone, we aim to explore whether increased parameter counts can further mitigate the topological hallucinations and dimensional drifts identified in our failure cases (Section F ). The 7B model is fine-tuned using a consistent LoRA configuration ( r = 8 , α = 32 r=8,\alpha=32 ) and identical progressive task-aware curriculum scheduling. Due to memory constraints, the batch size is appropriately adjusted while maintaining the same effective learning rate trajectory.
blocks.zh: 虽然我们的主要实验利用3B参数模型在性能和计算效率之间实现最佳平衡,但生成高度结构化的工程蓝图需要严格的逻辑推理和精确的坐标回归. 通过扩大骨干,我们的目标是探讨增加参数数是否能够进一步减轻在故障案件中发现的地形幻觉和维度漂移(F节)。 7B模式采用一致的LORA配置(r = 8,α = 32 r = 8,\ alpha = 32)和相同的渐进式任务意识课程时间安排进行微调. 由于内存限制,批量大小在保持相同有效学习速率轨迹的同时进行适当调整.

blocks.en: Table 7 summarizes the performance comparison between the 3B and 7B variants. Empirically, scaling up the model yields consistent improvements across all metrics. Most notably, in the Partial View Completion task ( { v iso , v front } → { v top , v right } \{v_{\text{iso}},v_{\text{front}}\}\rightarrow\{v_{\text{top}},v_{\text{right}}\} ), the 7B model achieves a substantial leap in Parameter Accuracy (from 75.53% to 82.82%) and a corresponding drop in Chamfer Distance (from 2.38 to 1.92). This indicates that the larger semantic capacity of the 7B model translates directly into finer coordinate regression and stricter cross-view geometric fidelity.

blocks.en: Beyond the quantitative metrics, the 7B model demonstrates enhanced robustness against the typical failure modes discussed in Section F . Specifically, the expanded context-processing capabilities significantly reduce counting errors for repetitive structures (e.g., arrays of circular holes), showcasing stronger local topological memory. Furthermore, the 7B variant exhibits tighter spatial constraints when inferring thin or elongated objects, reducing the coordinate drift that occasionally plagued the 3B model.

For conditional generation tasks, the model is evaluated only on the views that are required to be generated by the task instruction. For example, in the ISO-to-three-view task, the ISO view is treated as input and excluded from the target set, while the front, right, and top views are evaluated. Conversely, in the three-view-to-ISO task, only the ISO view is evaluated. For tasks conditioned on ISO and one additional orthographic view, the remaining two orthographic views are used as targets.

blocks.en: Zero123 produces raster images rather than SVG command sequences, so symbolic accuracy is not applicable to this baseline. To ensure a fair visual comparison, we evaluate Zero123 using the same raster-level protocol as our SVG outputs. Each predicted target view and its corresponding ground truth view are converted to RGB, composited on a white background when necessary, resized to the same 256 × 256 256\times 256 resolution, and evaluated per view. PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and CD are then computed with the same definitions and averaged over the same target views. For CD, foreground line pixels are extracted using the same grayscale thresholding rule and the same bidirectional Chamfer formulation. Thus, although Zero123 and DrawingsDreamer use different output representations, all reported visual metrics are computed under an aligned per-view image-space protocol.

blocks.en: While DrawingsDreamer demonstrates strong capabilities in generating multi-view engineering drawings, we observe certain limitations, primarily manifesting in two distinct failure modes as illustrated in Figures A4 , A5 .
blocks.zh: 绘图时 Dreamer在生成多视图工程图纸方面展现出强大的能力,我们观察到某些局限性,主要表现在图A4,A5所示的两种不同的失败模式中.

blocks.en: The first category of failure involves structural hallucinations, most commonly taking the form of incorrect inference regarding discrete geometric features. For instance, the model may occasionally generate an incorrect number of repeating elements, such as missing a circular hole or hallucinating an extra symmetric slot. We attribute this to the known limitations of purely autoregressive models when handling highly repetitive structural tokens over extended context windows. Without explicit counting mechanisms, the attention mechanism can occasionally lose track of repeating sub-sequences.
blocks.zh: 第一类失败涉及结构幻觉,最常见的形式是对离散几何特征的不正确推断。 例如,该模型偶尔可能会产生不正确的重复元素数量,如缺少一个圆形孔或幻觉产生额外的对称槽. 我们将此归因于纯自递性模型在处理扩展上下文窗口上高度重复的结构符号时已知的局限性. 没有明确的计数机制,关注机制偶尔会失去重复子序列的踪迹.

blocks.en: The second category pertains to precise spatial reasoning, which is particularly pronounced when the model attempts to generate flat, thin, or highly elongated objects. In these scenarios, the model can struggle to maintain rigorous dimensional consistency across multiple views, resulting in inaccurate lengths, irregular thicknesses, distorted hole radii, or misaligned spatial coordinates. This issue stems from the inherent challenges of mapping continuous, highly skewed geometric spaces into discrete token vocabularies. For extremely thin features, a minor coordinate drift or quantization artifact in one projection can be amplified during cross-view translation, compromising the strict spatial alignment required for professional CAD blueprints.
blocks.zh: 第二类涉及精确的空间推理,当模型试图生成平坦的,薄的,或高度延展的物体时,这种推理特别明显. 在这些假想中,模型可能难以在多种观点之间保持严格的维度一致性,导致长度不准确,厚度不规则,孔径扭曲,或空间坐标错位. 这一问题源于将连续、高度扭曲的几何空间绘制成单独的符号词汇的固有挑战。 对于极薄的特征,一个投影中的微小坐标漂移或定量文物可以在交叉视距翻译时放大,损害了专业CAD蓝图所需的严格的空间对接.

blocks.en: Addressing these limitations presents straightforward avenues for future research. While introducing explicit cross-view alignment rules could provide immediate structural constraints, a more scalable approach involves Reinforcement Learning (RL). By designing reward models that explicitly penalize cross-view geometric discrepancies, the framework can be optimized to internalize strict spatial alignment, preserving a purely data-driven sequence modeling paradigm without relying on hand-crafted heuristics.
blocks.zh: 克服这些局限性为今后的研究提供了直接的途径。 虽然采用明确的交叉观点统一规则可以提供即时的结构限制,但更可扩展的办法涉及加强学习。 通过设计明确惩罚跨视几何差异的奖励模型,可以优化框架,将严格的空间对齐内化,在不依赖手工制作的heuristic的前提下,保留纯粹由数据驱动的序列模型模式.

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope. Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A No or NA answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We mention our limitations in Appendix F . Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper has no limitation while the answer No means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not include theoretical results. Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We disclose all information needed for reproduction in Section 4 . Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a No answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We will provide data, code, and instructions for the final paper. Guidelines: • The answer NA means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so "No" is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We specifies all the training and test details in Section 4 . Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We report consistent performance across multiple runs and use fixed random seed settings to support the statistical significance of our results. Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer "Yes" if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We provide information about the computer resources used in Section 4.1 . Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We have read and understood the code of ethics and have made every effort to adhere to it. Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer No, they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [N/A] Justification: Our work contributes to Engineering Drawings Generation. It does not impact society at large. Guidelines: • The answer NA means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer NA or No, they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper poses no such risks. Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: All existing assets, including code, data, and models, are properly cited in the paper, and their licenses and usage terms are respected in accordance with the original sources. Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We will release our codebase along with detailed README files to ensure usability and reproducibility in an anonymous manner. Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: This work does not use crowdsourcing or human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: This work does not use crowdsourcing or human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [Yes] Justification: We describe the usage of LLMs in Section 3 and details in Section 4.1 . Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 抽象和导言中的主要主张准确地反映了该文件的贡献和范围。 准则: 答案NA意味着抽象和导言不包括文件中的主张。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 ● 审查人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的“不”或“NA”回答。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们在附录F中提到了我们的局限性。 • 答案NA表示,该文件没有限制,而答案是: 不表示文件有局限性,但在文件中没有讨论这些限制。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这种办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小来衡量。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文不包括理论成果. 指导方针: 答案NA表示论文不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们在第四节中披露复制所需的所有资料。 准则: • 答案NA表示论文不包括实验. ^ . 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将无法很好地看待这一问题: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式(如注册用户)限制对模型的获取,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码问题: 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要的实验结果? 答复:[是]理由: 我们将为最后文件提供数据、代码和指示。 • 答案NA表示,该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,所以"不"是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保留匿名性,提交人应公布匿名版本(如适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们具体说明了第4节中的所有培训和测试细节。 准则: • 答案NA表示论文不包括实验. ^ . 实验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便了解结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过附录中的代码或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们报告跨多个运行的一致业绩,并利用固定的随机种子设置来支持我们结果的统计意义。 • 答案NA表示论文不包括实验。 如果结果伴有错误栏,置信间隔,或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答"是". ^ 应明确说明错误条所捕获的变异因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应当加以解释(封闭的表单公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们提供关于第4.1节所用计算机资源的资料。 • 答案NA表示论文不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复:[是]理由: 我们阅读和理解了道德守则,并尽一切努力遵守守则。 • 答复NA意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答否,他们应当解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响? 答复:[不详]理由: 我们的工作促进了工程图画生成. 它并不影响整个社会。 • 答复NA表示已完成的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答NA或否,他们应当解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件没有涉及社会影响。 • 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(例如:造假、制造假貌、监视)、公平考虑(例如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多文件将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以让人们训练出更快生成Deepfake的模型.  • 作者应考虑在技术作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而造成的伤害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布具有高度滥用风险的数据或模型(例如,经过预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或报废数据集)而实施的保障措施? 答复:[不详]理由: 该文件没有这种风险。 准则: 答案NA意味着该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型,应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制使用该模型或实施安全过滤器。 • 支助 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 文件适当列举了所有现有资产,包括代码、数据和模型,并按照原始来源遵守了许可证和使用条款。 • 答案NA意味着该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件? 答复:[是]理由: 我们将公布我们的编码库以及详细的README文件,以确保匿名使用和复制。 准则: • 答案NA是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 人口集中和人类课题研究 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 答复:[不详]理由: 这部作品不使用众包或人文题材. 准则: 答案NA表示论文不涉及众包,也不涉及对人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)? 答复:[不详]理由: 这部作品不使用众包或人文题材. 准则: 答案NA表示论文不涉及众包,也不涉及对人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。 16. 关于LLM使用的声明问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明. 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们在第3节中描述了法学硕士的使用情况,并在第4.1节中详细说明。 指南: 答案NA是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及LLMs作为任何重要、原始或非标准组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: Claims
blocks.zh: 索偿

blocks.en: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
blocks.zh: 问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 抽象和导言中的主要主张准确地反映了该文件的贡献和范围。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A No or NA answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案NA意味着抽象和导言不包括文件中的主张。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 ● 审查人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的“不”或“NA”回答。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。

blocks.en: The answer NA means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper.
blocks.zh: 答案NA表示抽象和导言不包括论文中的说法.

blocks.en: The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A No or NA answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers.
blocks.zh: 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审查者不会很好地看待对这一问题的“不”或“NA”回答。

blocks.en: The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings.
blocks.zh: 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果能够归纳到其他环境。

blocks.en: It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.
blocks.zh: 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: We mention our limitations in Appendix F .
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 我们在附录F中提到了我们的局限性。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper has no limitation while the answer No means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced.

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)?

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a No answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer "Yes" if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer NA means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer NA or No, they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. blocks.zh: 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。

blocks.en: For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided.
blocks.zh: 对于来自某一特定来源(例如网站)的报废数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。

blocks.en: If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset.
blocks.zh: 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。

blocks.en: For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided.
blocks.zh: 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。

blocks.en: If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators.
blocks.zh: 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。

blocks.en: New assets
blocks.zh: 新资产

blocks.en: Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: We will release our codebase along with detailed README files to ensure usability and reproducibility in an anonymous manner.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 我们将公布我们的编码库以及详细的README文件,以确保匿名使用和复制。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.
blocks.zh: 准则: • 答案NA是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。

blocks.en: The answer NA means that the paper does not release new assets.
blocks.zh: 答案NA表示论文不释放新资产.

blocks.en: Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc.
blocks.zh: 研究人员应通过结构化模板,将数据集/代码/模型的细节作为其提交材料的一部分。 其中包括培训、许可证、限制等细节。

blocks.en: The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used.
blocks.zh: 文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。

blocks.en: At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.
blocks.zh: 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。

blocks.en: Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 与人类学科的众包和研究

blocks.en: Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: This work does not use crowdsourcing or human subjects.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 这部作品不使用众包或人文题材.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案NA表示论文不涉及众包,也不涉及对人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。

blocks.en: The answer NA means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects.
blocks.zh: 答案NA表示论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究.

blocks.en: Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper.
blocks.zh: 将这种资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主体,那么应在主要论文中尽可能详细.

blocks.en: According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.
blocks.zh: 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。

blocks.en: Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: This work does not use crowdsourcing or human subjects.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 这部作品不使用众包或人文题材.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案NA表示论文不涉及众包,也不涉及对人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。

blocks.en: The answer NA means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects.
blocks.zh: 答案NA表示论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究.

blocks.en: Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper.
blocks.zh: 根据开展研究的国家不同,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于). 如果你得到IRB的批准,你应该在报纸上清楚地说明这一点。

blocks.en: We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution.
blocks.zh: 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。

blocks.en: For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review.
blocks.zh: 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。

blocks.en: Declaration of LLM usage
blocks.zh: 声明LLM的使用

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required.
blocks.zh: 问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明.

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: We describe the usage of LLMs in Section 3 and details in Section 4.1 .
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 我们在第3节中描述了法学硕士的使用情况,并在第4.1节中详细说明。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer NA means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 指南: 答案NA是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及LLMs作为任何重要、原始或非标准组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。
